hook: POV: It's 1347 and your village just got its first case of the plague
premise: Day-by-day escalation from one cough at the market to quarantine, first-person dread throughout.
beats: Day 1: market, one merchant coughing, life normal
Day 3: church bells won't stop, doors marked
Day 6: your street, your neighbor, your door
notes: Launch video candidate. Part 2/3 built in. Visuals: medieval village, candlelight, fog — very generative-friendly.

hook: POV: You just boarded the Titanic in third class. You know the date. They don't.
premise: April 10, 1912 boarding day wonder → dramatic irony carries retention; ends night of the 14th, first shudder.
beats: gangway, luggage, awe at the ship
notes: Known ending = retention magnet. Launch candidate.

hook: POV: You survive Pompeii — hour by hour, August 24, 79 AD
premise: Timestamped countdown from a normal Roman morning to the pyroclastic flow; you make it out by boat.
beats: 1pm: the mountain opens, day turns to night

hook: POV: You're a plague doctor doing your rounds in 1665 London
premise: Inside the beaked mask for one night shift; what the herbs were for, what you could and couldn't do.
beats: dressing ritual: waxed coat, mask, herbs
first house call, chalk cross on the door
what you actually prescribe (and why it fails)
notes: The mask is a thumbnail/hook gift. Launch candidate.

hook: POV: A sword is forged for you, start to finish, in 1350
premise: Satisfying-process hybrid: ore to blade in first person, hammer rhythm as the audio spine.
notes: Tests the 'satisfying history' differentiator. Strong native-audio candidate.

hook: POV: You're a Roman legionary the night before the Teutoburg Forest
premise: 9 AD, rain, wrong roads, German scouts in the trees; dread build to the first arrow.
beats: veteran mutters about the guide Arminius
notes: History nerds amplify in comments (free engagement).

hook: POV: You're the food taster for a paranoid Roman emperor
premise: One banquet, every dish a coin flip; darkly comic tension format.
beats: morning briefing: who wants him dead this week
first course, the room watches you
notes: Loopable ending. Series potential: taster's diary.

hook: POV: You wake up as a Victorian chimney sweep. You're nine.
premise: One brutal workday, matter-of-fact tone doing the emotional work.
beats: first flue: too narrow, climb anyway
night: counting pennies, one bed, four boys
notes: Empathy engagement; pair with 'this was legal until 1875' overlay.

hook: POV: You're an Aztec merchant and Spanish ships just appeared on the horizon
premise: 1519 Veracruz coast; wonder before dread — floating mountains, men on deer.
beats: you're chosen to carry word to Tenochtitlan

hook: POV: Putting on a knight's armor takes 30 minutes. You have five.
premise: Process format with a clock: squires strapping you in as the battle starts without you.
beats: layer by layer, buckle by buckle
visor down, world narrows to a slit

hook: POV: You're a Viking on your first raid — and it goes wrong
premise: Lindisfarne-style landing subverted: fog, a bell, and the defenders were warned.
beats: shield wall forms ahead of you
notes: Subversion beats the saturated 'viking raid' baseline.

hook: POV: You're building the Great Pyramid — and you're not a slave
premise: Myth-busting day-in-life of a paid, fed, rotated laborer; bread-and-beer wages.
beats: work gang wakes, team names painted on stones
the ramp, the sledge, the water trick
your gang's stone slots in — 2.3 million to go

hook: POV: You're a 1920s bootlegger and the bar just got raided
premise: One night: false wall, password door, whistle, cellar escape through tunnels.
beats: cop at the peephole says the wrong word
tunnel exit into the alley — truck's waiting

hook: POV: The last day of a samurai, 1877
premise: Satsuma Rebellion's end; quiet ritual morning before the final charge at Shiroyama.
beats: dawn tea, armor older than you
notes: Emotional register test — saves/shares over laughs.

hook: POV: You're a medieval executioner and it's your first day
premise: The job nobody chose: inherited role, town that needs you and shuns you.
beats: father's ledger of names and prices
the crowd gathers, you check the blade twice
walking home alone, doors close as you pass
notes: Dark but historically grounded; strong comment bait ('the executioner also set bones — read more').
